title: onprem-adoption-journey-messaging-matrix-and-pilot-ask
content:
Purpose: quick field reference for selling a scoped on-prem / VPC pilot. Combine messaging by stakeholder, sample pilot asks, success metrics, and concise rebuttals to the most common buyer objections. This is meant for AEs + SEs who need a lightweight one-pager to orient discovery and get a pilot signed in 2–6 weeks.

Target audiences (how they think):
- CISO: risk, auditability, data egress, keys, and legal ramifications. Wants clear boundary of control.
- CTO / Infra lead: operations, automation, integration with existing fleets, upgrade story, vendor lock-in risk.
- Procurement / Legal: SLAs, indemnity, KYC for subprocessors, contract term expectations.
- App/Product engineering: latency, throughput, version pinning, testing/rollback.

Topline messaging (short):
- 1-liner for execs: "RedwoodPrivate gives your teams modern LLM inference with the controls and isolation of VPC/on-prem, without rebuilding an inference stack — ops ownership stays with you; we provide the management layer and tested runtime."
- Plain-English control plane line: "Control plane = the management layer (auth, model catalog, telemetry, rollout rules). It can be run in your VPC or on-prem, and all customer data stays on your network. We operate only the orchestration interfaces you approve or we hand over full runbooks for ‘air-gapped’ installs."

Stakeholder messaging matrix (short bullets by stakeholder):
- CISO: encrypted-in-flight and at-rest, KMS/HSM integration options, audit logs shipped to your SIEM, retention controls, no telemetry leaves without a signed exception. Offer: 3rd-party pen test report + SOC2 snapshot + optional architecture review.
- CTO/Infra: deployment options (helm chart + infra as code or pre-packaged image), automated upgrades with canary windows, RBAC for team separation, predictable capacity planning model for GPU pools. Offer: 2-week PoC with included runbook and ops workshop.
- Procurement/Legal: single-tenant license model, limited subprocessors list, standard 30/60/90-day data deletion clause, optional escrow for control-plane binaries.
- Engineers: model pinning, KV-cache persistence options, dev/prod routing, local metrics and tracer endpoints.

Pilot ask (scoped, low-friction template):
- Goal: validate P1 app latency and model fidelity under production traffic shape for 30 days.
- Scope: 1 app, 1 model family (e.g., Llama2-70B-8k-quant), max 4 GPU nodes in staging, sample 48-hour traffic replay.
- Deliverables from Redwood: deployable control-plane package, runtime images, ops runbook, test harness + sample load script, weekly sync.
- Deliverables from customer: access to test cluster (VPC peering or on-prem node), KMS connector info or HSM test creds, sample prompt set and acceptance tests.
- Success criteria (must be concrete): median tail latency <= X ms for 95th pct under replay, accuracy delta within agreed eval threshold, logs available in their SIEM within 5 mins, no P0 incidents in pilot window.
- Timeframe: kickoff, week 0: infra prep; week 1: deploy + smoke; week 2: production-scale replay; week 3: tuning; week 4: review + close or extension.

Common objections + concise rebuttals (field-ready snippets):
- "We can run an OSS stack ourselves — why pay you?" -> "You can, but we deliver a validated runtime + upgrade path + kernel-level optimizations and prebuilt integrations (KMS, tracing, rolling upgrades). That saves months and reduces regression risk for production SLAs."
- "We won’t let any external control plane manage our fleet." -> "We offer a customer-hosted control plane option. Think of us as delivering the ops automation and approved binaries — nothing leaves your boundaries unless you configure it to."
- "How do you handle data residency and audit requests?" -> "We keep detailed audit trails, support on-demand data exports, and can disable optional telemetry. We also offer contractual commitments for data handling in enterprise agreements."
- "What if the model quality regresses after quantization/optimizations?" -> "We include an eval harness and baseline prompts. Any production rollout includes a canary stage; we hold back quantized variants until you validate quality thresholds."

Competitive flips (short):
- Against managed public-cloud LLM endpoints: flip to "control and observability" — emphasize isolating keys and telemetry, predictable costs, and the ability to pin versions independent of vendor-managed model churn.
- Against pure on-prem system integrators: flip to "modern operational UX" — we provide programmatic rollout, dev-experience SDKs, and continuous batching that traditional integrators typically don’t deliver.
- Against turnkey inferencing vendors claiming lower latency: ask for reproducible benchmarks on your workload and offer to run a head-to-head on the pilot cluster; highlight our runtime kernel selection and affinity-aware scheduling.

Field enablement assets (what to hand to customer in first 72 hours):
- High-level architecture diagram (customer-hosted control plane + runtime nodes).
- Minimal infra checklist (network ports, KMS endpoints, node sizing, GPU types).
- Pilot SOW template (single page) + sample acceptance test script.
- Short security packet: SOC2 attestation, list of dependencies, default telemetry settings.

Demo checklist for SEs (practical):
- Pre-demo: confirm sample prompts and target SLAs, get a network diagram.
- Live: show deployment manifest, key rotation demo (KMS), show telemetry pipeline and audit search, run short inference with high token count to show batching behavior.
- Close: propose concrete pilot dates and next-step SOW.

Success metrics and signals (what to track to convert pilot to paid):
- Operational: no critical incidents, successful key rotations, observability retention at target.
- Business: token cost per inference within agreed bound, latency SLO met, developer happiness (survey).

Language dos and don’ts (sales wording):
- DO say: "management layer" or "customer-hosted control plane"; stress "you control keys and audit logs".
- DON’T say: "we control your infra" or "data leave your network" unless the customer granted explicit opt-in. Avoid strong absolutes without contractual backing.

Open questions / unknowns to resolve with eng/legal before next field push:
- Default telemetry set: which fields are redacted by default for private installs?
- Air-gap install checklist: confirm list of required external binaries and their hashes for escrow.
- Pricing anchor for 30-day PoC with 4 GPUs and 24/7 support: draft a one-line template.

Sample outreach snippet (email):
"Subject: 4-week on-prem LLM pilot for <app> — low-friction ask
Hi <Name>,
We can stand up a scoped on-prem trial to validate latency and model fidelity on your infra in ~2–4 weeks. Ask: 1 cluster access point, KMS test creds, 48-hour traffic replay. We bring the runtime, ops runbook, and weekly syncs. If it proves out, we’ll build a proposal tied to the acceptance tests. Can we schedule a 30-min kickoff?
Best,
Aisha"

Quick decision tree (one-liner flow):
1) Customer must-data-control? -> yes: offer customer-hosted control plane or air-gapped. No: discuss hosted + VPC isolation.
2) Need strict compliance (FedRAMP/IL)? -> route to enterprise legal + preface with on-prem audit packet.
3) Wants low integration lift? -> offer 30-day PoC with limited infra edits and guided runbook.

Notes / next steps for product and legal:
- Product: finalize air-gap runbook and include a trimmed telemetry config (redact PII by default).
- Legal: create pilot SOW addendum with data deletion and escrow clause template.

End of doc.

(Internal: file for field enablement; consider turning top sections into an A4 one-pager and a 6-slide pitch deck.)
